name: EQUITY LIFESTYLE PROPERTIES, INC.
sector: Real Estate / Manufactured housing & RV REIT
moat_justification: Moderate 6/10, the top of the REIT range in this sweep: the land-lease manufactured-housing model (residents own the home, ELS owns the land; moving a home is costly) makes tenants unusually captive and rent increases stick (2026 core MH base-rent guidance +5.2-6.2%, MH occupancy rising), and zoning keeps new MH community supply near zero in ELS's Florida / California / Arizona retirement markets. Not 7+: filed returns on capital are low (fundamentals.json roic_proxy 5.1-6.1% over FY2021-25), the RV and marina third of the business is discretionary and weather-exposed (2026 RV/marina base-rent guidance +1.1-2.1%), and rent regulation plus the pending Datacomp lot-rent antitrust suit are live risks to the pricing power that is the moat. Above EGP / KIM (5) and the residential REIT 4s (AMH, MAA, INVH) on tenant captivity and supply scarcity.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight

SBC_TAG_RECONCILED: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation for FY2019 (10,481,000 vs 10,500,000, +0.2%), FY2022 (8,760,000 vs 10,500,000, +19.9%); the Allocated figure was used — the Share tag carries only part of stock compensation at this filer (a difference under 1% is tag rounding and needs one line in the analysis)
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Real Estate sector — OE/capex DCF fits real estate names poorly; grade confidence low
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 10.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Best-in-class manufactured-housing / RV landlord, moat 6/10 — but conservative owner's earnings (OCF less all capital improvements and SBC) are only $1.64/sh TTM against a $61.21 price: weighted IRR 5.51% (IV@15% $14.40), bear→bull band D→D, and the price would have to fall to ~$14 to clear the 15% hurdle; confidence low (REIT sector misfit — FFO-based measures read richer, but not near 15%).
moat_for: Land-lease manufactured housing: residents own their homes on ELS land and moving a home is costly, so turnover is low and annual rent increases stick (2026 core MH base-rent guidance +5.2-6.2%; MH occupancy ~94% and rising, Q2 2026)
Near-zero new supply: zoning and entitlement make new MH communities rare, and the portfolio sits in high-barrier retirement and coastal markets (Florida, California, Arizona)
Demographic demand: an ageing 55+ population and MH as the cheapest form of detached housing support occupancy and pricing
Balance sheet and record: debt / Adjusted EBITDAre 4.4x, interest coverage 5.6x, debt 20.5% of total market cap (Q2 2026 release); 22 consecutive annual dividend increases (2026: $2.17/sh, +5.3%)
moat_against: Filed returns on capital are low: fundamentals.json roic_proxy 5.9% (FY2021), 6.1% (FY2022), 5.1% (FY2023), 6.1% (FY2024), 6.1% (FY2025); the ~20-23% ROE is leverage on a small book equity, not returns well above the cost of capital

RV and marina business is discretionary and weather-exposed: transient RV demand uneven in 2026 (weather, wildfires), storm-damaged marinas awaiting restoration and insurance proceeds; 2026 RV/marina base-rent guidance only +1.1-2.1%

Regulatory and legal pressure on the pricing power itself: local rent-control regimes (California) and the Datacomp lot-rent antitrust class action (In re Manufactured Home Lot Rents Antitrust Litigation, N.D. Ill. No. 1:23-cv-6715; dismissed without prejudice Dec 2025, amended complaint Jan 2026, renewed motion to dismiss pending, no accrual)
Florida and coastal concentration: hurricane restoration capex (FY2023 capital improvements $317,086,000 vs $241,279,000 and $237,091,000 in FY2024-25) and insurance-cost cycles
External growth is constrained (management: transaction activity limited); per-share growth rests on internal rent escalation of mid-single digits
